newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Iraq's Uday has bullet in spine - opposition.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Uday has bullet in spine - opposition.

text.p: Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday has had a bullet lodged in his spine since an assassination attempt in December, an opposition group said in remarks published in Kuwait on Saturday.

"A French medical team has refused to conduct surgery to remove a bullet that settled in Uday's spine," Bayan Jabr, a member of the Supreme Council for the Islamic Revolution in Iraq (SCIRI), was quoted as saying by al-Rai al-Aam newspaper.
The team did not explain the reason for declining to operate on Uday, said Jabr. Iraqi doctors said such surgery involved high risk, he added.

"Gangrene started to form in the left leg of Uday. There is a possibility of amputating the infected part," added Jabr, a representative in Damascus for SCIRI, a Shi'ite Moslem group with a Tehran-based chief.
"It (the team) has removed 10 bullets from his (Uday) body," said Jabr.

Uday told a visiting Palestinian cleric from his hospital bed early this month that four bullets were still lodged in his body following the attempt on his life when unidentified gunmen opened fire on his car in Baghdad.
France said last Sunday that Uday would not be given medical treatment on its soil. A French foreign ministry spokesman did not give a reason for France's decision.
According to unconfirmed reports, a French medical team went to Baghdad to see Uday in December shortly after the shooting.
